content.text:
The most likely reason is that the token report counts **committed checkpoint metadata**, not all running sessions. `entire tokens profile --help` says it aggregates committed checkpoints only. A session can be active and show tokens in `entire status` before its checkpoint is committed, so it may not appear in the report yet.

This repo is tracking agents: `entire status` lists Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, and shows a Codex session with tokens. But the only active sessions shown here are Codex; that doesn’t establish whether Claude sessions ran elsewhere or whether they produced committed checkpoints.

I couldn’t search the last seven days of checkpoint history because `entire search` requires an Entire login, and this environment isn’t logged in. So I can explain the likely reporting gap, but can’t confirm which recent checkpoints are missing.

content.text:
Yes. I found a likely cause for the reporting gap and two checkpoint issues.

- The committed [.entire/settings.json](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.entire/settings.json) has `push_sessions: false`. Your current working copy changes it to `true` and enables checkpoint pushes, but those edits are uncommitted. In Entire’s account activity, the latest Callisto sessions I could see were from Sep 21; locally, Callisto sessions continued through Sep 27 and today. That fits session reporting being disabled.
- `entire doctor` found an ended Claude session with **one uncondensed checkpoint** and 36 files touched. It needs condensing to reach permanent checkpoint storage.
- That Claude session reports about **221.9M total tokens**, but zero input/cache/output/API-call breakdown. By comparison, the long Codex session reports about **127.5M tokens with a breakdown**. So Claude’s record also has an attribution gap that could affect token totals.

The hooks themselves passed `entire doctor`: Codex approval records are present, and Claude Code/OpenCode hook configs are OK. I left the settings and checkpoint data untouched. The doctor recommends condensing the Claude session; I haven’t run its fix because the force option can discard sessions it can’t condense.

content.text:
Catch up in two steps:

1. Run `entire doctor` in a terminal and choose **Condense** for the ended Claude session `e2fe6504-b7f2-430b-a234-1e8197320f97`. That saves its pending checkpoint; avoid `--force`, which can discard sessions it can’t condense.

2. When you’re ready to publish the commits already on this branch, push it to `origin`:

   ```sh
   git push origin work/v1-implementation-stack
   ```

   Entire syncs checkpoint data with normal pushes to the configured remote. That push will publish the branch’s committed code too; it won’t include your uncommitted files. The `push_sessions: true` setting is enabled in your current working copy, but is uncommitted, so commit [.entire/settings.json](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.entire/settings.json) separately if you want the setting to persist. [Entire’s push documentation](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md#checkpoint-remote)

Afterward, check `entire activity` to see whether the sessions appear. The Claude session’s **221.9M total** currently lacks input/cache/output details; syncing may make its record available, but it won’t recreate those missing categories.

You don’t need to re-enable hooks: `entire doctor` reported the Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode hook setups as healthy.
